texts.facts: Plaintiff's case: 1. Brief facts of the case are that the plaintiff is residing at 2 nd floor of the suit property i.e. E-11, Kalkaji, New Delhi (hereinafter referred to as "suit property"). It is cla imed that defendant no.2 is the owner of ground floor of the suit property and has rented it out to defendant no.1 who is running an eating outlet by the name of Burger Dr. Vibhore Sharma vs The Burger Club Etc on 27 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197381493/ 1 Club from the ground floor. It is claimed that the defendant no.1 has installed additional two water tanks over the gate of the suit property, which is used by the plaintiff also to access his property at the second floor. It is claimed that the defendant no.1 & 2 had also encroached the public lane outside the suit property by installing iron staircase. It is further claimed that the two additional water tanks installed by defendant no.1 overflows leading to water logging at the common gate of the suit property. It is further stated that a water purifier system has also been installed on the wall along with the additional water tanks, for which the electricity wires for the doorbell switch were removed without consent of the plaintiff and also left open. It is claimed that such actions of defendant no.1 have resulted in endangering the suit property as well as obstructing the passage of the plaintiff to his property on second floor. Hence, plaintiff has prayed for a decree of mandatory injunction in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants thereby directing the defendant no.3 to remove encroachment from public lane caused by defendant no. 1 & 2 by installing their equipment's, i.e. AC, AC ducts, iron stair cases, water purifier systems, etc. in the public lane of property E-11, Kalka Ji, New Delhi-110019 and a decree for permanent injunction in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants thereby restraining the defendant no. 1 & 2, their agents, employees, assignees, representative or any other person on their behalf, from encroaching the public lane by installing their equipment's and placing their goods and temporary structure towards public lane at property bearing No. E-11, Kalka Ji, New Delhi-110019. Defendant's case: 2. Written statement has been filed by previously impleaded defendant no. 1 (Burger Club) in which the allegations of the plaintiff have been denied. It is claimed by Burger Club that they have given the franchise of burger club food services private Ltd. to G & G Industries on dated 27th July 2021. As per the agreement the defendant no. 1 have no legal concern in shop G-1, E-11, Kalka ji main road Delhi as the franchise belongs to G & G Industries. The copy of the agreement is also placed on record. In view of the submissions made by previously impleaded defendant no. 1 (Burger Club), G.G. Industries was impleaded as a defendant in the present suit vide order dated 25.03.2022 and previously impleaded defendant no. 1 (Burger Club) was deleted from the memo of parties vide order dated 01.10.2022. 3. Written statement has also been filed by defendant no.2 and it is stated that he is the owner of a commercial shop at the ground floor of the property bearing no. E-11, Kalkaji, New Delhi. It is claimed that the entire renovation work was carried alongside the wall of the property of himself and it has no concern with the property of the plaintiff. The said renovation work was objected and obstructed by the plaintiff on various occasions, since he was not able to park his car alongside the wall of the defendant no.2, which resulted into repeated altercations between the plaintiff and defendant no.1. It is submitted that the plaintiff instead of pressing his relief against defendant no. 2 who was allegedly creating nuisance for him, himself committed Dr. Vibhore Sharma vs The Burger Club Etc on 27 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197381493/ 2 illegality by closing the valves of the water tanks installed on the terrace resulting into interruption of regular water supply of the defendant no.1 from the overhead water tanks belonging to the defendant no.2, and blocked the access to the terrace, which is a common facility to all the owners of the building. When the defendant no.1 apprised about non-availability of water supply and no access to the common terrace, the defendant no.2 intervened and tried to resolve the Issue between the defendant no.1 and the plaintiff, however the plaintiff did not adhere to the requests of the defendant no.2. 4. In absence of water supply, the defendant no.1 was unable to run his business and in order to make temporary arrangements, the defendant no. 1 had to install two water tanks alongside the balcony of the first floor. Since the entire arrangement was inconvenient for the defendant no.1, the defendant no.2 had to approach the Hon'ble court by filing a civil suit no. 716/2021 titled "Amrit Ahuja versus Vibhor Sharma", for enforcement of his civil rights, wherein interim relief was granted by the court of Ld. CJ, South East District, Saket thereby directing the plaintiff herein to immediately open the water valves, however no orders was passed to secure the access to the defendant no.2 to the overhead water tanks. Aggrieved by the order, the plaintiff started complaining of regular water overflow from the temporary water tanks, to resolve the issue, the defendant no. 2 requested the plaintiff herein to allow him to access the overhead water tanks so that an automatic water sensor in the water tanks may be installed and the problem of overflow of the water may be avoided. The plaintiff herein allowed the defendant no.2 and an automatic water sensor was installed on the overhead water tanks. Thereafter there is no water overflow from the overhead water tanks. It is further claimed that the said water tanks have been installed much below the second floor of the suit property and is within the portion of the ground floor, in which the plaintiff has no right, title or interest. It is also denied that any hazardous situation was created by exposing any electricity wires for installation of the water tanks or the water purifier system. 5. Defendant no.3/MCD has also filed its written statement in which it is stated that with respect to encroachment at public land in the form of temporary iron staircase and iron box in lane is concerned, they were demolished/removed during encroachment removal programme. However, the water tank, AC ducts on projection of first floor still exists and the same is monolithic with the building. Status Report of Defendant no.3. 6. In the status report filed by defendant no.3 it was averred that the water tanks installed by way of temporary structure on wall of first floor are unauthorized and not permissible. It is further stated in the said status report that there are deviations in the shape of excess coverage at all floors including basement. Apart from excess coverage, there are projections on government land at first and second floor level, which are non-compoundable. 3 Issues:- OPD 4 5) Relief. In order to prove his case, the plaintiff had examined himself as PW1. In his examination-in-chief, he mostly reiterated the averments made in the plaint and relied upon the following documents: Sl . No . Exhibits/Marks Documents 1. Ex. PW-1/1(OSR) Aadhar Card of the deponent and employee card of the deponent. 2. Ex. PW-1/2(OSR) Copy of mutation in MCD. 3. Mark-A Copy of partition deed of the family (page 18 to 27) 4. Mark-C Photographs of illegal encroachment of public lane. Mark-E Copy of complaint made by Resident Welfare Association to SHO Kalkaji 8. Despite opportunity given, the defendant no.1 did not cross examine PW1 and stopped appearing before the court. Hence, defendant no.1 was proceeded as ex-parte vide order dated 03.10.2023. 9. Plaintiff has also examined Sh. Saurabh Shukla as PW2, who presented the complaint received vide emails dated 17.03.2021 and 18.03.2021 to RWA, E-block, Kalkaji vide Ex.PW2/1 and action upon the complaint vide Mark PW2/3 and he was not cross examined by the defendants no.2 & 3 despite opportunity given. 10. Plaintiff has also examined Sh. Jawahar Khan as PW3, who also presented the complaints dated 16.03.2021, 18.03.2021 and 23.03.2021 vide Ex.PW3/1 and he was not cross examined by the defendants no.2 & 3 despite opportunity given. Thereafter, vide separate statement of Ld. Counsel for the plaintiff, PE was closed on 21.11.2023.
texts.arguments: Before moving ahead, I would like to refer to the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in case titled as Rajender Motwani & Anr. Vs. MCD & Ors. RSA No. 243/17 decided on 16.10.2017 wherein, it was observed and held as follows:- "the second reason for rejecting the arguments urged on behalf of the appellants/plaintiffs is that an illegal construction in itself does not give any legal right to a neighbour. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Canara Bank and Ors. Dr. Vibhore Sharma vs The Burger Club Etc on 27 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197381493/ 7 v. Debasis Das and Ors AIR 2003 SCW 1561 held as: "A person who seeks equity must come with clean hands. He, who comes to the Court with false claims, cannot plead equity nor the Court would be justified to exercise equity jurisdiction in his favour. A person who seeks equity must act in a fair and equitable manner." 19. The Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Kimti Lal Rahi v. Union of India, AIR 1993 Delhi 211, has held that: "16. [I]t is well settled that one who claims equity must do equity. Estoppel springs from equity doctrine. If the application at the principal leads to results which are unjust and opposed to fair play and justice the doctrine will have no application in a given case." 20. In the case of Champa Arora & Ors. vs. Shiv Lal Arora and Ors. 2001 VII AD (Delhi) 602, Hon'ble High Court of Delhi held as under:- "It is a settled law that a person, who seeks equity, must come with clean hands. A litigant who suppresses a fact from the court, indeed loses the right to seek an equitable relief of ad interim injunction". 21. Further reliance may be placed upon the law laid down in M/s Seemax Construction (P) Ltd. v. State Bank of India, AIR 1992 Delhi 197 and Mahabir Prasad Jain v. Ganga Singh, AIR 1999, SC 3873. It has been held in Executive Committee of Vaish Degree College, Shamli v. Lakshmi Narain AIR 1976 SUPREME 888 that the relief of injunction is purely discretionary and the plaintiff cannot claim it as a right. The relief has to be granted by the Court according to sound legal principles and ex debito justice. The Court has to administer justice between the parties and cannot convert itself into an instrument of injustice or an engine of oppression. The Dr. Vibhore Sharma vs The Burger Club Etc on 27 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197381493/ 8 The doctrine of preponderance of probabilities was discussed in the judgment titled Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research v. Jaspal Singh, (2009) 7 SCC 330 which reads as under: "17. In Syad Akbar v. State of Karnataka (1980) 1 SCC 30 this curt dealt with in details the distinction between negligence in civil law n din criminal law. It has been held that there is marked difference as to the effect of evidence, namely, the proof, in civil and criminal proceedings. In civil proceedings, a mere preponderance of probability is sufficient, and the defendant is not necessarily entitled to the benefit of every reasonable doubt; but in criminal proceedings, the persuasion of guilt must amount to such a moral certainty as convinces the mind of the court, as a reasonable man, beyond all reasonable doubt". 24. In Dr. N.G. Dastane Vs. Mrs. S. Dastane on 19th March, 1975 AIR 1975 SC 1534, (1975), SCC 326, Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under: "24. The normal rule which governs civil proceedings is that a fact can be said to be established if it proved by a preponderance of probabilities. This is for the reason that under the Evidence Act, Section 3, a fact is said to be proved when the court either believes it to exist or considers its existence so probably that a prudent man ought, under the circumstances of the particular case, to act upon the supposition that it exists. The belief regarding the existence of a fact may thus be founded on a balance of probabilities. A prudent man faced with conflicting probabilities concerning a fact-situation will act on the supposition that the fact exists, if on weighing the various probabilities he links that the preponderance is in favour of the existence of the particular fact. As a prudent man, so the court applies this test for finding whether a fact in issue can be said to be proved. The impossible is weeded out at the first stage, the improbable at the second. Important issues like those which affect the status of parties demand a closer scrutiny than those like the loan on a promissory note: "the nature and gravity of an issue necessarily determines the manner of attaining reasonable satisfaction of the truth of the issue "Per Dixon, J. In Wright v. Wright (1948) 77 C.L.R. 191 at p. 210; or as said by Lord Denning, "the degree of probability depends on the subject- matter. In proportion as the offence is grave, so ought the proof to be clear" Blyth v. Blyth (1966) 1 A.E.R. 534 at 536. But whether the issue is one of cruelty or of a loan on a pronote, the test to apply is whether on a preponderance of probabilities the relevant fact is proved. In civil cases this, normally, is the standard of proof to apply for finding whether the burden of proof is discharged."
